text:
I am the Shadowy One, the widower, the unconsoled,
Prince of Aquitaine, whose tower is gone;
my only star has died, and my starry lute
bears within it Melancholy’s black sun.

In the night tomb, you who comforted me,
restore Pausilippo and the Italian sea,
that flower so dear to my desolate soul,
and the vine where tendril twines with rose.

Am I Amor or Phoebus? Lusignan or Byron?
My brow still reddens from the Queen’s kiss;
I dreamed in the Grotto where the Siren swims…

Twice victorious, I have crossed Acheron,
sometimes playing on Orpheus’ lyre
the Saint’s sighs, at others the Fairy’s cries.

translation.title: The Disinherited
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
